Actually, looking more carefully - the blocks were at cols 39-40 (blue) and 41-42 (sky blue). After pressing LEFT, they're still at the same position. So LEFT doesn't move them when they're at the right end?
Wait, earlier when I pressed LEFT, the blocks moved from right to left. But now they're stuck. Let me check - maybe the game over state changed something about the blocks.
Actually, I think the issue is that the game over state put the blocks in a "locked" position. Or maybe the blocks can only move one direction at a time and need to be "unlocked" first.
Let me try RIGHT first to see if they move, then LEFT.
Actually wait - I need to reconsider the entire puzzle. The blocks are at the RIGHT end. When I moved them LEFT earlier, they went to the notch and got stuck. When I moved them RIGHT, they went to the far right and triggered game over.

- Rows 21-22: gap (notch) at cols 17-22, then continues from col 23 to col 38
When blocks are vertical (4 tall, rows 19-22), they can't pass through the notch because rows 21-22 have a gap.
When blocks are horizontal (2 tall), they could potentially pass through if positioned at rows 19-20.
But how do I make blocks horizontal AND position them at rows 19-20?
Let me try: DOWN to make horizontal, then check position, then LEFT.

# Try DOWN to make blocks horizontal, then check position
result = action(['DOWN'])
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
for n in nodes:

        min_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
        max_r = max(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
        max_c = max(p[1] for p in b)
        print(f"Block {n['color']}: rows {min_r}-{max_r}, cols {min_c}-{max_c} (h={max_r-min_r+1}, w={max_c-min_c+1})")
